source.title: Meta Dropout: Learning to Perturb Latent Features for Generalization
source.authors: Haebeom Lee; Taewook Nam; Eunho Yang; Sung Ju Hwang

record.file_problem: None noted; the supplied text includes the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a learned latent-feature regularizer on few-shot classification tasks, an extension of the claim's generalization topic to a meta-learning setting.
record.gate_note: The paper measures few-shot test accuracy for Meta-dropout and comparison methods. Its findings do not test the listed claim versions: Meta-dropout is a learned meta-regularizer, and the experiments do not test random-label fitting, ordinary dropout, or the other version-specific conditions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a learned, input-dependent noise generator for few-shot meta-learning. It discusses dropout and generalization, but its own results do not test V1–V8. Meta-dropout and the Gaussian-noise ablations do not establish the stated effects of ordinary dropout in V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: Meta-dropout improves few-shot generalization and generally outperforms the tested perturbation regularizers, while also improving adversarial robustness. This should not imply uniform superiority: Meta-SGD's miniImageNet 5-shot accuracy is unchanged at 65.55%, and additive Meta-dropout exceeds the multiplicative version on Omniglot 5-shot.
record.recipe_differences: Learns input-dependent multiplicative noise through meta-learning for few-shot classification; the claim versions concern ordinary training and different interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance differs across dataset and shot conditions. The paper reports that additive noise works well on Omniglot but is somewhat suboptimal on miniImageNet; input-independent and fixed noise variants do not outperform base MAML, and learned input-dependent variance underperforms the fixed-variance Meta-dropout.

fits_no_version.finding: Meta-dropout raises MAML accuracy from 95.23 to 96.63 and 98.38 to 98.73 on Omniglot, and from 49.58 to 51.93 and 64.55 to 67.42 on miniImageNet, for 1-shot and 5-shot respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Meta-learned input-dependent feature perturbations can improve few-shot classification accuracy in the tested transductive MAML setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The PGD evaluations report improved adversarial robustness with Meta-dropout, with smaller differences on miniImageNet than Omniglot.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Meta-dropout can improve adversarial robustness without explicit adversarial training in these few-shot tasks.

record.problems: The experiments concern few-shot meta-learning rather than standard training on natural labels; the testing framework is transductive via batch normalization. Some comparisons are taken from reported performances. Adversarial accuracy results are plotted rather than tabulated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows extracted for Table 1's repeated baseline/model comparisons, Table 2's mixup and information-theoretic comparator variants, Table 3's full noise-generator ablation, or figure-only adversarial-accuracy curves. The central Meta-dropout versus no-perturbation results are retained in Table 2; Table 3 repeats those same Meta-dropout values.

untested.parts: No comparison of random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to fit training data.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison; Adam and SGD serve different optimization levels.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No ordinary-dropout comparison, dropout-rate sweep, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. Learned Meta-dropout is a different intervention.
No magnitude-aware weight sharpness measurement or ranking against generalization gaps.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence.

record.verdict_notes: The numerical values in R1–R12 match the supplied tables. The omitted comparisons and adversarial curves are declared in rows_left_out, and none supplies a missing test of V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
Tests Meta-dropout, a learned input-dependent meta-regularizer, rather than standard dropout or the stated dropout and weight-decay conditions.
